mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.50 percentage points over three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.50% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6.0% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.0% in a single month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, signaling weak wage growth and muted consumer spending, which results in flat or negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market normalization with weak wage growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE also rises in the same month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).
